speaker: Doctor
text:
That is very helpful. To better understand the connection between your fever, wrist pain, and skin lesions, how long have these symptoms been present?

Also, have you noticed any swelling in your hands or joints, or any difficulty moving your fingers?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota, have you had any direct contact with ticks or noticed any tick bites? Also, do you have a current rash or any other skin lesions besides what you mentioned?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: CBC (Complete Blood Count), ESR, CRP, and Ferritin. REQUEST IMAGES: High-resolution photos of the violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on your wrists and hands.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever (RMSF). The combination of fever, severe monoarticular wrist pain/swelling, and characteristic violaceous vesiculopustular lesions is highly suggestive of RMSF, despite the previous misdiagnosis of iron deficiency anemia. Immediate doxycycline treatment is indicated.
